page: Hetzner Cloud ccx33 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC processor family and virtualized via QEMU. The server provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 31.0 GB, yielding a balanced ratio of 3.91 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly with a 240 GB local NVMe SSD, while no integrated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded throughput, with the instance scoring in the top 25 percent for both stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core runs. Geekbench text processing reaches the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression also demonstrates upper-quartile speed. In multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU benchmarks, performance aligns solidly within the median range. Tradeoffs appear in memory bandwidth under large uncached read workloads (256 MB block sizes at 38.5 GB/sec) and medium model LLM prompt ingestion, which fall into the lower quartile.

The dedicated vCPU allocation eliminates noisy-neighbor CPU contention, providing consistent compute execution compared to shared or burstable alternatives. Given its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration, strong single-core benchmarks, and bundled high-speed NVMe storage, Hetzner Cloud ccx33 is well positioned for medium-scale application databases, Redis caching layers, web serving platforms, build pipelines, and transactional production backends.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx33 is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 8 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, 31.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 240 GB local NVMe SSD. Built on the x86_64 architecture without discrete GPU acceleration, it maintains a balanced allocation of roughly 3.91 GB of memory per core. In benchmarks, ccx33 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25 percent for stress-ng and Geekbench single-threaded tests, alongside top-tier text processing. Multi-core compute and PassMark database operations place within the median tier, though uncached large-block memory read bandwidth remains comparatively modest. The dedicated CPU resource provisioning prevents core sharing contention, delivering predictable compute density. These hardware specifications make the instance technically suitable for production relational databases, Redis key-value workloads, CI/CD runners, and steady web application serving.
